<question>
In the lease fl-lease-03, clause 9 lets the landlord change the locks and have the water and electricity shut off if the rent is more than five days late. Is that allowed in Florida?
</question>

<answer>
No. Under Florida law, a landlord may not cause, directly or indirectly, the termination or interruption of any utility service furnished to the tenant, whether or not the landlord controls or pays for that service [1]. A landlord also may not prevent the tenant from gaining reasonable access to the dwelling unit, for example by changing the locks [1].

A landlord who does either of these things is liable for actual and consequential damages or three months' rent, whichever is greater, together with court costs and attorney's fees [1].
</answer>

<reference>
No. A landlord may not cause, directly or indirectly, the termination or interruption of any utility service furnished to the tenant, whether or not he controls or pays for it, and may not prevent the tenant from gaining reasonable access to the dwelling unit, for example by changing the locks (Fla. Stat. s. 83.67(1) and (2)). A landlord who does so is liable for actual and consequential damages or 3 months' rent, whichever is greater, and costs including attorney's fees (s. 83.67(6)).
</reference>
